symptom: An ALTER PAGE that only inserted widgets also changed a combobox it did not touch: the one combobox whose 6 screen-reader texts had no translation in the project's second language gained them, copied from the 3 comboboxes beside it that had them. check and mx check clean; the diff showed an unrequested change.
cause: ALTER PAGE edits the stored BSON in place, so the untouched combobox came back byte for byte. But the insert shifted every path, which turns positional pairing off, and a pluggable widget's texts sit under its Properties list, which turns named-element pairing off. That left the source-string pairing, which keyed the untouched English-only text on (en_US, 'Clear selection') and handed it the Dutch of the other comboboxes' texts with the same English.
fix: A text that holds a stored text's $ID is that text, so it is never paired by source. carryTranslationsByID, after the transplant, is the carry for a text paired by $ID. A text the rebuild minted afresh is still paired by source.
insight: Source-string pairing is a guess, and correct only for a text that has no identity of its own. Before falling back to it, ask whether the element already has an exact pairing (its $ID survived), and if so do not guess. Measured on 11.14.0: a page with two comboboxes, Dutch stripped from comboBox2's unit, and ALTER PAGE insert of one dynamic text. Before the fix comboBox2 gained 6 nl_NL translations; after, 0, and comboBox1 kept its own. mx check reports the same CE0463, which my strip caused, before and after.
test: modelsdk/canon/translations_untouched_2587_test.go (untouched English-only text stays English-only, plus the control that a freshly minted text is still paired by source); failed before (the untouched text gained nl_NL)
